layers.process: Tibetan settlements at Bylakuppe (Dickey Larsoe and Lugsung Samdupling), Mundgod (Doeguling), Kollegal (Dhondenling) and Hunsur (Rabgayling), and the Atisha Charitable Trust land near Mysuru, are Restricted Areas under the Fourth Schedule of India's Immigration and Foreigners Order 2025. Daytime visits are allowed without a permit if the settlement, monastery or institute gives the visitor's name, parentage, date of birth, nationality, passport and visa numbers to the Foreigners Registration Officer. Staying needs a Restricted Area Permit; foreign students can get one valid for 3 years if the institute vouches for them.

Daria Daulat Bagh, Srirangapatna: the Archaeological Survey of India lists this monument among its ticketed sites. Check the relevant entrance, price, ticket availability, local opening hours and any applicable exemptions with the monument authority before a visit; the listing alone does not confirm that the site is open.

laws.rule: Under the Karnataka Prevention of Slaughter and Preservation of Cattle Act 2020, cattle means a cow, calf, bull or bullock of any age and a buffalo under 13 years old (section 2). No one may slaughter cattle (section 4), transport them for slaughter inside the State (5) or out of the State (6), or buy or sell them for slaughter (7). A buffalo over 13 years may be slaughtered with the competent authority's certificate (section 18).
laws.penalty_signal: Slaughter (section 12(1)): 3 to 7 years or a fine of INR 50,000 to 5 lakh per animal (about A$746 to A$7,457), or both. Other breaches (12(2)): 3 to 5 years or a fine of INR 50,000 to 5 lakh, or both.

laws.rule: Under the Karnataka Excise Act 1965, section 14, no one may possess any intoxicant above the limit the State Government sets by notification, except under a licence or a permit. The quantity limit is in the notification, not in the Act text; check it with the Excise Department before carrying more than a few bottles.
